body.en:
Question B-006-006-002.

Why the correct answer is right: An antenna tuner is an adjustable matching network. It transforms the impedance presented by the antenna system into a load the transceiver can drive properly; it does not physically retune the antenna wire.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It helps a receiver automatically tune in stations that are far away": Automatically finding distant stations is a receiver tuning or scanning function; an antenna tuner works on the radio-frequency (RF) load impedance, not on station selection.
- sourceIndex 2: "It switches an antenna system to a transmitter when sending, and to a receiver when listening": Switching between transmit and receive is done by a T/R relay or switching circuit; a tuner does not perform the send/listen changeover.
- sourceIndex 3: "It switches multiple transceivers to a common transmission line and antenna": Selecting among multiple radios or antennas is the job of an RF switch; a tuner changes impedance, not which transceiver is connected.
